chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man from whose urethra something comes out after he has performed ghusl. He said: "He performs ghusl and repeats the salat, unless he had urinated before performing ghusl, in which case he does not repeat his ghusl."

Muhammad said: Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Whoever performs ghusl while in janabah before urinating, then later finds moisture, his ghusl has been invalidated. But if he had urinated and then performed ghusl, then later found moisture, it does not invalidate his ghusl; rather, he must perform wudu (ablution), because the urine did not leave anything behind."

key_terms.إِحْلِيلِهِ: his urethra, the organ from which the discharge exits
key_terms.الْبَوْلَ: urination, mentioned here as affecting the legal ruling
key_terms.بَلَلًا: moisture or wetness found after ghusl
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.غُسْلُهُ: his ghusl, the ritual bath he performed

ai.seo_question: If moisture comes out after ghusl from janabah, must the ghusl and salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling concerning moisture that exits after ghusl from janabah. If a person did not urinate before ghusl and then finds moisture, the ghusl is invalidated; but if he urinated before ghusl, the ghusl remains valid, though wudu (ablution) may still be required. The narration is significant in Shi'i fiqh for rulings on ritual purity and the distinction between what nullifies ghusl and what necessitates wudu (ablution).
